title: Generation of bright quantum high-order harmonic driven by combined coherent and bright squeezed vacuum light
authors: Wentao Wang, Yaoshun Sun, Liyuan Wang, Lingrui Hu, Dajun Ding, Xiangyu Tang, Mingxuan Li, Jianmin Yuan, Sizuo Luo
abstract: Attosecond quantum light, formed by the superposition of high-order harmonics driven by intense quantum light, opens new routes to probe quantum-mechanical correlations in matter. In this study, we have investigated the macroscopic propagation effects of quantum high-order harmonics generated by the combination of strong coherent and weak bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) lasers interacting with atomic gas. Our results reveal that the pressure-dependent intensity of harmonics arising from absorbing or emitting BSV photons differs from that of harmonics generated using only strong coherent pulses. Macroscopic propagation simulations indicate that the action phase of harmonics is perturbed by the weak BSV pulses. This perturbation modulates the phase mismatch of sub-cycle attosecond bursts and affects their quantum properties when the gas pressure varies. The ability to generate bright quantum high-order harmonics lays a foundation for the establishment and application of attosecond quantum spectroscopy.
summary: This paper explores generating bright quantum high-order harmonics by combining intense coherent lasers with weak squeezed vacuum light interacting with atomic gas. The key finding is that the BSV field introduces unique spectral components and perturbs the phase matching condition based on gas pressure. This capability paves the way for advanced attosecond quantum spectroscopy.
main_problem: The study investigates the macroscopic propagation effects of quantum high-order harmonics (QHHG) generated by combining strong coherent laser light with weak bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) light interacting with atomic gas.
main_result: The inclusion of BSV light generates novel spectral features (half-integer and even harmonics) whose optimal generation pressures differ significantly from those driven by coherent light alone, allowing for quantum control over XUV sources.
method: The research combines experimental measurements using an XUV spectrometer with theoretical simulations employing a wave-mixing model to account for macroscopic propagation effects.
model_or_system: The system involves HHG in Krypton gas driven by a two-color field: a strong coherent laser (800 nm) and a weak BSV field (1600 nm). The theory models the phase mismatch perturbation caused by the action phase shift induced by the BSV light.
key_observables: Harmonic spectra ($	ext{H}_{2N+1}$, $	ext{H}_{(2N+1)\pm 1/2}$, $	ext{H}_{2N}$), gas pressure dependence of harmonic intensity, and the second-order correlation function $g_2(0)$.
important_parameters: Gas pressure (5 to 60 Torr); BSV quantum statistics ($g_2(0) = 2.324$); relative intensities of different harmonic components.
main_assumptions: The theoretical model assumes that the macroscopic propagation can be analyzed by incorporating the perturbation from the weak BSV field into the phase-matching condition.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic setups, pressure dependence of various harmonic components showing distinct optimal pressures, and simulated spectra validating the theory against experiment.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the physical system (coherent + BSV driving), detailing the theoretical framework (wave-mixing model, action phase perturbation), presenting experimental results on spectral features vs. pressure, and concluding with the implications for quantum spectroscopy.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems as it demonstrates how non-classical light sources (BSV) can be used to engineer and control fundamental nonlinear processes like HHG in a medium, moving beyond standard coherent driving assumptions.
